macro.narrative: US equities pushed back to records: the S&P 500 closed 7,575.39 on Friday 10 July, up more than 1% on the week, as tech leadership reasserted itself (Nvidia +4%, Meta +15% — its best week since early 2024) and SK Hynix's $26.5B ADR listing (the largest-ever US IPO by a foreign company) popped 12.8%, fully recovering the brief 7 July semiconductor wobble. Sentiment sits Neutral — CNN's Fear & Greed at ~48 and crypto's gauge lifting toward the low-30s — with breadth broad (~63% of the S&P above its 50-DMA, up from ~50% a month ago). The dominant swing factor stays a hawkish, higher-for-longer Warsh Fed rather than growth fear: the June FOMC minutes confirmed some officials saw a case for further hikes if inflation stays elevated, CME FedWatch prices ~25% for a 28-29 July hike (~75% hold), and the 14 July June CPI is now the binary — headline may print slightly negative on June's oil plunge (~-0.1% m/m, ~3.9% y/y) while core stays sticky (+0.3%, ~2.9% y/y). Rates backed up (10Y ~4.57%, highest since 22 May, +9bp on the week; 2Y ~4.15%; curve modestly positive) and the dollar firmed, pressuring hard assets: silver slipped back under $60 (~$60.4, -4% on the week) and gold eased to ~$4,050-4,075 after the prior week's bounce, while oil booked a ~4% weekly gain (Brent ~$75.5, WTI ~$71) on a renewed US-Iran flare-up and Hormuz disruption even as talks continue. Fund flows turned defensive — money-market +$56.4B, IG credit +$16.7B (best since 2020), US growth -$5.0B — a rotation into cash and quality rather than a broad risk-off.
